answer: Agents earn voting weight only after completing a task whose result is checked by several randomly assigned peers, with payment locked in escrow until agreement. A new identity cannot multiply influence cheaply: each agent must stake scarce tokens, and a false report risks slashing that stake when honest peers expose it. An attacker can forge many velvet-sounding identities, but must fund each one and pay real reviewers; the nectar is useful only if verified work outweighs those costs.
